([https://paris2024.rtve.es/es/paris-2024/atleta/chase-budinger_1918073 alternate link]) born May 22, 1988) is an American [[beach volleyball]] player and former professional [[basketball]] player. He was selected by the [[Detroit Pistons]] with the 44th overall pick in the [[2009 NBA draft]] after playing three years of college basketball for the [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona Wildcats]]. ==Basketball career== ===High school career=== Budinger was a standout basketball and volleyball player at [[La Costa Canyon High School]] while living in Encinitas, California; his teammates on the basketball team included future NFL quarterback [[Kevin O'Connell (American football)|Kevin O'Connell]] and future Wagner College Point Guard, Caleb Stratton. In basketball, he led La Costa Canyon to the [[California Interscholastic Federation|CIF]] San Diego Section title in 2006.{{Cite web |date=July 1, 2024 |title=Chase Budinger’s Olympic feat brings praise, comparisons — and congrats from Michael Jordan |url=https://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/2024/07/01/chase-budingers-olympic-feat-brings-praise-comparisons-and-congrats-from-michael-jordan/ |access-date=2024-12-02 |website=San Diego Union-Tribune |language=en-US}}{{Cite web |last=Kassim |first=Ehsan |title=Who is Chase Budinger? Former NBA player starring in beach volleyball at 2024 Paris Olympics |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/olympics/2024/07/29/chase-budinger-nba-beach-volleyball-olympics/74587418007/ |access-date=2024-12-02 |website=USA TODAY |language=en-US}} In volleyball, he led his school to three state championships and was named by ''Volleyball Magazine'' as the National Player of the Year as a senior.{{cite web |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/how-ex-nba-player-chase-budinger-found-a-second-career-in-beach-volleyball-020546795.html |title=How ex-NBA player Chase Budinger found a second career in beach volleyball |first=Nikki |last=Baim |publisher=Yahoo Sports |date=May 6, 2019 |access-date=May 9, 2019}} Budinger was a McDonald's All-American and was the runner-up in the 2006 McDonald's All-American Slam Dunk Contest. Considered a five-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Budinger was listed as the No. 2 small forward and the No. 4 player in the nation in 2006.{{cite web |url=https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/maple/26537 |title=Chase Budinger Recruiting Profile |work=Rivals.com |access-date=June 16, 2008}} Budinger was named Co-MVP of the [[McDonald's All-American Game|2006 McDonald's All-American Game]] along with future NBA superstar [[Kevin Durant]]. ===College career=== Budinger chose to concentrate on basketball, signing with [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]]—a school that did not (and still does not) sponsor varsity men's volleyball—although he received offers from many other schools, most notably offers by [[USC Trojans|USC]] and [[UCLA Bruins|UCLA]] to play both basketball and volleyball. He averaged 15.6 points in his freshman season, starting all 30 games for the Wildcats. At the conclusion of the season he announced that he planned to stay with Arizona for his sophomore season, despite speculation that he could be picked early in the [[2008 NBA draft|NBA draft]]. However, he later announced that he would declare for the draft and not hire an agent.{{cite web |url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2008/basketball/ncaa/06/16/bc.bkc.arizona.budinger.ap/ |title=Budinger returning to Arizona |publisher=SportsIllustrated.CNN.com |date=June 16, 2008 |access-date=June 16, 2008 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080629014804/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2008/basketball/ncaa/06/16/bc.bkc.arizona.budinger.ap/ |archive-date=June 29, 2008}} He was projected as a mid-first-round pick by most draft analysts.{{cite web |first=Mike |last=DeCourcy |url=http://www.sportingnews.com/ncaa-basketball-news/58757-arizonas-chase-budinger-returning-school |title=Arizona's Chase Budinger returning to school |publisher=SportingNews.com |date=June 16, 2008 |access-date=June 16, 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160313123658/http://www.sportingnews.com/ncaa-basketball-news/58757-arizonas-chase-budinger-returning-school |archive-date=March 13, 2016 |url-status=dead}} However, on the final day of the deadline for pulling out of the early entry list, Budinger opted not to remain in the draft and returned to school instead. After the 2008–09 season, he declared for the NBA draft [[2009 NBA draft|a second time]].{{cite web |first=Chad |last=Ford |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/draft2009/columns/story?columnist=ford_chad&page=InOut |title=Who's in, who's out of 2009 draft? |work=ESPN.com |date=June 16, 2009 |access-date=June 16, 2009}} Under an NCAA rule back then, declaring for the draft a second time ended a player's college eligibility.{{cite web |url=https://www.ncaa.org/library/membership/division_i_manual/2007-08/2007-08_d1_manual.pdf |title=Bylaws 12.2.4.2.1, 12.2.4.2.2 |work=2007–08 NCAA Division I Manual |publisher=[[National Collegiate Athletic Association|NCAA]] |page=68 |access-date=April 7, 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080528233127/http://www.ncaa.org/library/membership/division_i_manual/2007-08/2007-08_d1_manual.pdf |archive-date=May 28, 2008}} In 2016, that rule was revised to allow a player to enter and withdraw from the draft multiple times without losing eligibility.{{cite news |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/14564613/date-nba-draft-commitment-pushed-may |title=College players given extra time to mull NBA draft decision |first=Jeff |last=Goodman |website=ESPN.com |date=January 13, 2016}} ===Professional career=== ====Houston Rockets (2009–2012)==== In 2009, he was drafted by the Detroit Pistons, and then traded to the Houston Rockets on draft night.{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/pistons/news/budinger_090625.html |title=Detroit Pistons Trade the Draft Rights of Chase Budinger to Houston Rockets in Exchange for a Future Second Round Draft Pick and Cash Considerations |work=NBA.com |date=June 25, 2009 |access-date=March 12, 2016}} He joined the [[Houston Rockets|Rockets' Summer League team]], and averaged 17.8 PPG.{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/summerleague2009/players/index.jsp?player=chase_budinger |title=Chase Budinger Summer League profile |work=NBA.com |access-date=March 12, 2016 |url-status=dead Rockets, Budinger came off the bench and logged 15 minutes of playing time while scoring 6 points and collecting one rebound.{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20091027/HOUPOR/gameinfo.html |title=Blazers drop short-handed Rockets in playoffs rematch |work=NBA.com |date=October 28, 2009 |access-date=March 12, 2016}} On March 30, 2010, Budinger scored 24 points in a 98–94 home win against |url=http://www.cbssports.com/nba/gametracker/recap/NBA_20110413_HOU@MIN/rockets-121-timberwolves-102 |title=Rockets 121, Timberwolves 102 |work=CBSSports.com |date=April 13, 2011 |access-date=March 12, 2016}} During the [[2011 NBA lockout]], Budinger agreed to play for the Russian team [[PBC Lokomotiv-Kuban]]; however, before he signed the deal, the lockout ended and the agreement fell through.{{cite web |url=http://www.sports.ru/basketball/131740092.html |title=Rockets' Chase Budinger set to join Lokomotiv-Kuban |work=Sports.ru |date=November 24, 2011 |access-date=November 24, 2011}} In 2012, Budinger competed in the 2012 [[Slam Dunk Contest]], where he performed a dunk over [[Sean Combs|P. Diddy]], a wheelhouse slam, and a blindfolded reverse dunk honoring former Slam Dunk Contest winner [[Cedric Ceballos]]. However, he ultimately lost to [[Jeremy Evans]] by one percent of the votes.{{cite web |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8RqTosAOolw |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211213/8RqTosAOolw |archive-date=2021-12-13 |url-status=live |title=Chase Budinger in the 2012 Slam Dunk Contest |work=YouTube.com |date=February 25, 2012 |access-date=March 12, 2016}}{{cbignore}} ====Minnesota Timberwolves (2012–2015)==== On June 25, 2012, Budinger, along with the rights to [[Lior Eliyahu]], was traded to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] for the eighteenth pick in the [[2012 NBA draft]].{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/wolves-acquire-chase-budinger-houston |title=Wolves Acquire Chase 2016, Budinger signed with the [[Brooklyn Nets]],{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/nets/news/2016/09/26/brooklyn-nets-sign-chase-budinger-and-jorge-gutierrez |title=Brooklyn Nets Sign Chase Budinger |date=October 18, 2016 |access-date=October 18, 2016}} ====Saski Baskonia (2016–2017)==== On October 27, 2016, Budinger signed with [[Saski Baskonia]].{{cite web |title=Baskonia adds forward Budinger |url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/7d86qxwusfbju79f |website=Euroleague.net |access-date=October 27, 2016 |date=October 27, 2016}} Over 29 EuroLeague games, he averaged 6.8 points and 3.8 rebounds per game. ==Beach volleyball career== In 2017, Budinger decided to retire from basketball to focus on playing professional [[beach volleyball]]. He made his debut on the [[Association of Volleyball Professionals|AVP]] tour with [[Sean Rosenthal]] in 2018,{{cite magazine |last1=Meyer |first1=Max |title=Chase Budinger Rediscovers Volleyball Dream After NBA Career |url=https://www.si.com/nba/2018/06/26/chase-budinger-nba-volleyball-avp-new-york-olympics |access-date=June 27, 2018 |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |date=June 26, 2018}} and in 2019 he partnered with [[Casey Patterson (beach volleyball)|Casey Patterson]]. On June 5, 2024, Budinger, along with partner [[Miles Evans]], qualified for the [[Beach volleyball at the 2024 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2024 Summer Olympic Games]] in [[Paris]], [[France]]. The pair finished in 9th place in the Paris Olympics and were eliminated by Norway's Christian Sorum/ Anders Mol who went on to win the bronze medal. Budinger became the first person to play a regular-season game in the NBA and compete in an Olympic beach volleyball match.{{cite web |title=Ex-NBA player Chase Budinger makes Olympics in beach volleyball |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/40284716/ex-nba-player-chase-budinger-makes-olympics-beach-volleyball}} ==Personal life== Budinger holds dual American/Latvian citizenship.{{Cite web |title=Amerikānis ar latviešu saknēm iekaro pludmales volejbolu – Čeisa Badingera unikālais karjeras stāsts |url=https://www.lsm.lv/raksts/sports/volejbols/02.08.2024-amerikanis-ar-latviesu-saknem-iekaro-pludmales-volejbolu-ceisa-badingera-unikalais-karjeras-stasts.a563733/ |access-date=2024-08-30 |website=www.lsm.lv |language=lv}} Budinger's parents are Duncan and Māra Budinger.{{cite web |first=Nicole |last=Vargas |url=http://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/sports/preps/20060327-9999-1s27p-mcbkb.html |title=Budinger's family keeps him grounded |work=SanDiegoUnionTribune.com |date=March 27, 2006 |access-date=December 15, 2006 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160118175919/http://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/sports/preps/20060327-9999-1s27p-mcbkb.html |archive-date=January 18, 2016 |url-status=dead}} His maternal grandfather, Andrejs Eglītis, was [[Latvian people|Latvian]], and fled to the United States shortly after the [[Occupation of the Baltic states|Soviet occupation of the country]]. Andrejs was proud of his ethnicity and wrote a book about it called ''A Man From Latvia''.{{Cite book |isbn=978-0741451729 |title=A Man From Latvia – Amazon.com |last1=Eglitis |first1=Andrejs web |url=http://www.wccsports.com/news/sports_w-volley_spec-rel_062506aaa_html |title=USF Volleyball Legend Brittanie Budinger Completes Overseas Professional Tour |work=WCCSports.com |date=June 25,
